speaker: Jennifer Cullison
words: This interview is being conducted for the California State University  Stanislaus Office of Communications and Public Affairs and for Dr. Jennifer Cullison's oral history research.

speaker: Jennifer Cullison
words: The interviewer is myself, Jennifer Cullison. The narrator is Donna Pierce.

speaker: Jennifer Cullison
words: The interview is taking place at California State University Stanislaus on October 13, 2023.

speaker: Jennifer Cullison
words: Donna Pierce is an important citizen of this campus for many reasons. The Office of Communications and Public Affairs plans to interview her multiple times.

speaker: Jennifer Cullison
words: Today's interview will focus on her leadership and passion in the development of one of the campus's most fascinating projects, the

speaker: Jennifer Cullison
words: Wayne and Donna Pierce Trans-California, Pathway, which has its origins in the 1980s.

speaker: Jennifer Cullison
words: So, to start off, Donna, can you tell us about yourself before your life in Turlock, where you grew up, where you went to school, how you met Wayne?

speaker: Donna Pierce
words: Yes. I actually met Wayne when

speaker: Donna Pierce
words: I was eight and he was ten and we had both gone to the cafeteria to listen to the World Series - Yankees and Dodgers - in 1952.

speaker: Donna Pierce
words: I, to this day, don't know why I was there but he clearly was a baseball fan and so I, taking his example, I became a lifelong Dodger fan.

speaker: Donna Pierce
words: But the lucky thing about me was my best friend was his cousin so I got invited to many birthday parties and barbecues and family events.

speaker: Donna Pierce
words: And I knew at a very young age that was the guy that I wanted to be associated with.

speaker: Donna Pierce
words: We both went to a Atascadero Union High School in a town of about 4,000 at that time.

speaker: Donna Pierce
words: It's only 40,000 now. But we he was a very active in all the sports on campus and a leader in the leader in the student government.

speaker: Donna Pierce
words: And I was a so-so student but I did graduate.

speaker: Donna Pierce
words: And I was also interested in the sports so, in fact, I used to sit in the stands while he played third base for Atascadero High with one other fan.

speaker: Donna Pierce
words: And we got to be good friends too.

speaker: Donna Pierce
words: But I was a fan of Wayne's. He went to Cal Poly for a year where he played college baseball and then he transferred to Humboldt State to graduate study.

speaker: Donna Pierce
words: He wanted to be a forest ranger. I graduated and went to UC Santa Barbara for two years.

speaker: Donna Pierce
words: When he graduated in 1963.. [196]4, we got married and moved to Washington State University where we both studied.

speaker: Donna Pierce
words: I got my masters... my bachelor's degree and Wayne got his Masters and PhD in 1971.

speaker: Donna Pierce
words: And Turlock was... At the time there weren't too many jobs when he was ready to graduate.

speaker: Donna Pierce
words: There was a job in New Haven, Nashville, Reno, and Turlock.

speaker: Donna Pierce
words: And I worked nights and I got caught in a snow drift one night and I woke him up and said,

speaker: Donna Pierce
words: "Call New Haven, Nashville, and Reno because we are through with snow."

speaker: Donna Pierce
words: And he came to Stanislaus State so happy to have a view of Half Dome, to be close to the Valley, to be in the Valley and to be close to Yosemite, which meant so much to him.

speaker: Jennifer Cullison
words: Thanks for sharing that.

speaker: Jennifer Cullison
words: The next question we have is - What was it like being the spouse of a faculty member in the 1970s and 1980s, especially, or over the lifespan [time] that when you and your husband were here together?

speaker: Jennifer Cullison
words: Was there still, for example, a Faculty Wives Club in the early 1970s? Were you involved in that?

speaker: Jennifer Cullison
words: And what can you tell us about what came of that organization or of the early years?

speaker: Donna Pierce
words: Well, it was an very exciting time when you consider, Jennifer, that there were four buildings here.

speaker: Donna Pierce
words: And I think two of them were brand new when we got here: the classroom, the gym, the theater, and the library.

speaker: Donna Pierce
words: And I like to say I was taller than all the trees there but of course then I was 5'4.

speaker: Donna Pierce
words: And there was always kind of a whiff of fertilizer in the air.

speaker: Donna Pierce
words: But the university or actually the college [at that point] had hired about 40 faculty and staff in those early years ofthe late 60s and 70s and we were all young.

speaker: Donna Pierce
words: We all had young children. We were all energetic.

speaker: Donna Pierce
words: We were all wanting to build something really wonderful here and for the most part everybody who came did stay here.

speaker: Donna Pierce
words: We were very active. And you ask about the Faculty Women's Club.

speaker: Donna Pierce
words: They were... They were actually kind of an impetus for us to put together picnics... potlucks.

speaker: Donna Pierce
words: We would do barbecues when we put on a prom. We had many activities on the campus that built the morale

speaker: Donna Pierce
words: and the camaraderie. And the fact that so many of these people have stayed here these...

speaker: Donna Pierce
words: I've been here.... 52 years. And it tells you that this was a wonderful place to raise a family.

speaker: Donna Pierce
words: And we did enjoy growing this university. The Faculty Women's Club was very important in a way.

speaker: Donna Pierce
words: All the women associated with the college were invited to join - like we had staff and faculty and wives (mainly wives) and that helped one another.

speaker: Donna Pierce
words: I remember I got a letter from the president Pat Rasmuson in 1971 saying if I need... needed any help before my furniture arrived or other items that you need to survive in the beginning of a new school year that they could.

speaker: Donna Pierce
words: They had a pantry that could provide things that you could borrow. And we always had interesting speakers.

speaker: Donna Pierce
words: We had great community involvement. We would do rummage sales to raise scholarship money.

speaker: Donna Pierce
words: And it was a very active club. And then in the late 80s I think, more and more people were going to work and we were meeting at night.

speaker: Donna Pierce
words: And so I'm thinking that people were maybe caught up with their work, their families, [feeling] tired and apparently the membership faded.

speaker: Donna Pierce
words: But I we [Wayne and I] had gone to Washington DC for a year on a sabbatical. And the club was disbanded at that time in 1987.

speaker: Donna Pierce
words: And I've always regretted that because I thought it was just a good way for all of us to get together [and] help one another.

speaker: Donna Pierce
words: We had a bridge club where I learned to play bridge  and which I do today. So I... I'm sorry that we didn't have that but we did have an awful lot of fun building this university.

speaker: Jennifer Cullison
words: Thank you. So you... I can't recall if you specifically said, right, that Wayne started his position in Fall of 71.  So that's when you came here?

speaker: Donna Pierce
words: Mhm [Yes].

speaker: Jennifer Cullison
words: So a little more than a decade after the university [college] started.

speaker: Donna Pierce
words: Yes.

speaker: Jennifer Cullison
words: I still am not sure if  there was actually a Faculty Wives Club but by the time you were here it was the The Women's Club, which makes good sense. Faculty Women's Club. And, yes. I don't know when it had started but  it clearly was in... it had been in business for a while because they were well established.

speaker: Jennifer Cullison
words: And you had told me before a story about how the women in that club were challenged by the students, I think, for a touch football game.

speaker: Jennifer Cullison
words: Do you want to tell us that story?

speaker: Donna Pierce
words: Yes, we were. Thank you for remembering that because that was really quite a remarkable story. I... the student.. women students on the campus challenged the faculty women to a football game.

speaker: Donna Pierce
words: And so I gathered everybody I could imagine. And as I said, we all were young.

speaker: Donna Pierce
words: We all had toddlers when we would show up for our practices at Crane Park.

speaker: Donna Pierce
words: And we were not that successful in the game. And so I decided we definitely needed a rematch.

speaker: Donna Pierce
words: And so I started calling people the next year and the first person I called said, "Oh, I'd like to but I'm pregnant."

speaker: Donna Pierce
words: And the next person I called said, "Oh, I would like to but I'm pregnant."

speaker: Donna Pierce
words: And the third person I called said the same thing. And when I got to the fourth person who said, "I would like to but..." , I said, "I know. You're pregnant."

speaker: Donna Pierce
words: And she said, "I'm at the doctors. Tom doesn't even know yet!"

speaker: Donna Pierce
words: So, needless to say, we never got our rematch. But it was really kind of a fun time for all of us.

speaker: Jennifer Cullison
words: Right. For the context for the listeners like this is still this period, I mean, just actually 71 - seven years after... seven years after the end of the baby boom. But, sure enough, people are still having kids.

speaker: Donna Pierce
words: Oh, yes, they were. I don't know if the football game was the reason for it [laughter].

speaker: Jennifer Cullison
words: But, so tell us a little bit about your involvement with the campus in different ways, just to give people a sense of, you know, your wide reaching impact beyond the trail and then we'll talk about the trail.

speaker: Jennifer Cullison
words: So maybe a little bit about the basketball timekeeping [shot clock operating], anything related to sports.

speaker: Donna Pierce
words: Well, you know, I told you that  Wayne was quite an athlete and I always wanted to be one but I was born way too soon before Title 9 and I'm actually a left... natural lefty.

speaker: Donna Pierce
words: But I learned to do everything right-handed by watching.

speaker: Donna Pierce
words: But I got a job as a teacher in the California Youth Authority where we incarcerate our children.

speaker: Donna Pierce
words: And I would come home from Stockton and Wayne would say there's a ball game: basketball, soft not softball but basketball or um whatever activities were on the campus including the music, the theater.

speaker: Donna Pierce
words: Anything that was happening on campus - we were there.

speaker: Donna Pierce
words: And at the time, the basketball players played their games at Turlock High School and in 1978 we got our own gym.

speaker: Donna Pierce
words: And we always had a fall tournament at Thanksgiving in which we had eight teams - four men and four women teams - playing in a tournament.

speaker: Donna Pierce
words: And on the first night the table res dissolved because it takes a lot of people to run basketball games.

speaker: Donna Pierce
words: And people had other obligations and had to leave.

speaker: Donna Pierce
words: And so the athletic director came in the stands and said, "Can you run a shot clock?"

speaker: Donna Pierce
words: And I said, "Well, I never have but I'll practice on the next game and be ready for the our game."

speaker: Donna Pierce
words: And he said, "Well you have to be perfect the first time." Well, I can tell you, Jennifer, I was not perfect but I must have been good enough because I did it for about 20 years.

speaker: Donna Pierce
words: And then I did another well no 30 years.

speaker: Donna Pierce
words: And then I did another 10 years at scorekeeper at the .. basketball games.

speaker: Donna Pierce
words: And I also was the first softball coach here and I was a much better shot clock operator than a softball coach.

speaker: Donna Pierce
words: But I was proud of the fact that we kept our obligations and we met the teams we were supposed to meet.

speaker: Donna Pierce
words: And that's a whole other chapter  of my life that I mostly have tried to forget but we have had very successful basket(ball), baseball, [and] softball teams.

speaker: Donna Pierce
words: In fact, tomorrow we're going to honor the team from 2004 that is in the Hall of Fame... [that is] going to be inducted into the Hall of Fame.

speaker: Donna Pierce
words: So, Wayne,  for his part, he became the NCAA representative at Stanislaus State. And in that role, he monitored eligibility.

speaker: Donna Pierce
words: He worked on getting postgraduate scholarships for these athletes.

speaker: Donna Pierce
words: He traveled with them. He gave many exams in airports and hotel rooms and worked with these young student athletes.

speaker: Donna Pierce
words: And because of that I was able to also travel to some postseason events that were just spectacular and meant so much to me.

speaker: Donna Pierce
words: And I like to talk about the athletic part of our lives because so many of these people who came here in the... particularly [in] the 80s in the early 80s, are the people who support me to this day people who came here, took jobs in hospitals, corporations mostly school teachers, counselors, and principal.

speaker: Donna Pierce
words: And now they're retiring now but we're still we're all still very close.

speaker: Donna Pierce
words: And so I credit that with the fact that I was so happy to be around healthy young people after spending my day with troubled youth and it's just been a wonderful richness for me and all aspects of this university mean everything to me.

speaker: Donna Pierce
words: The growth of the physical plant and the programs here is just to me mind-boggling - from these humble beginnings.

speaker: Jennifer Cullison
words: Thanks for sharing that. I think offline I'm going to have to talk more about some of these things as relates to my research.

speaker: Donna Pierce

speaker: Donna Pierce

speaker: Donna Pierce

speaker: Donna Pierce

speaker: Donna Pierce
words: trees. And I'm sorry I can't.. I've spoken to Ina [Gotelli] about this but she kind of remembers the beginning as part of this museum idea but I can't give you any more information on that.
